assessment.rationale: Kernel-time shares are read straight from the profiler's own summation and are robust to the co-tenancy that makes the idle-fraction claim shakier, since shares are internally normalised. Risk of bias low for that reason. What the shares do NOT establish is how much is recoverable: torch.compile has already fused some of these, so the headroom is an open measurement rather than a deduction.

metrics.name: kernel_time_share
metrics.result: RMSNorm 18.6% + other elementwise 8.1% = 26.7% of kernel time in memory-bound work; 45.4% is already cuBLAS/nvjet GEMM and is the hardest share to improve.

locators.excerpt: GEMM (nvjet) 45.4% / 30,363 launches; FlashAttention 19.6% / 5,728; RMSNorm (triton) 18.6% / 10,653; other triton elementwise 8.1% / 32,071; softmax+cross-entropy 7.7% / 2,327. The two log_softmax/nll_loss kernels are the largest per-instance in the profile at 4.79ms and 4.28ms, together 9.1ms per optimizer step.

scope.budget: 300 charged training seconds on one H200, scope karpathy_228791f_corrected_bpb_h200_train300s_v2c
scope.model: decoder-only transformer, 8 layers, d_model 512, 4 heads of 128, SSSL window pattern

statement: RMSNorm and small elementwise Triton kernels together account for about 26.7% of GPU kernel time and about 42,000 of the ~102,000 kernel launches per profiling window, which is a memory-traffic and launch-count cost rather than useful matmul work.
